text:
Ava (CEO): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands  threading answers here for mission/positioning/competitor questions. Keep Qs short and tag owners.

Nadia (VP Product): Does "serving is the advantage" become external messaging or stay internal?

Ava (CEO): Use externally but with a line of context. Example: 'As models evolve, the winner is the team that consistently delivers inference with predictable latency, cost, and controls.' Pair with a customer proof point.

Sam (Sales): Sales needs a 1-line to use in discovery vs clouds  something that lands with infra founders.

Ava (CEO): Try: 'Redwood makes inference predictable and economical at production scale
across hosted, reserved, and private deployments.' Shorten as needed.

Yara (Marketing): Competitor guidance: can we do named comparisons in mid-funnel collateral?

Rafael (CTO): Avoid naming in public materials. Mid-funnel trusted docs can include direct comparisons but route through legal. Prefer anonymized reproducible benchmarks + workload case studies.

Omar (Infra): For Dedicated SLAs: can we confirm numbers so Sales can quote them?

Rafael (CTO): Dedicated: target 99.9% monthly uptime for reserved pools; Hosted paid tiers 99.5%. Latency SLOs documented per instance family.

Nadia (VP Product): Docs ask: parity checklist for Hosted vs Private  who owns that and when?

Ava (CEO): Nadia + Rafael to own the checklist. Publish a short matrix next week and an FAQ for customers explaining staggered feature cadence.

status-bot: Note: parity-matrix draft uploaded to /docs/internal/positioning/parity-draft-v1.md

Sam (Sales): One last: can Eng provide a tiny table of batching impact ranges for sales calls? even ballpark numbers help.

Rafael (CTO): We'll provide typical ranges (short/med/long sequences) with caveats; dropping into this thread by EOD.

Ava (CEO): Thanks all
we'll consolidate the press blurb, sales one-liners, and parity matrix here when ready. :sparkles:
